title: Report a score map through BiConsumers

blocks.text: `Map.forEach` takes a `BiConsumer<K, V>`: it hands each key and value as two arguments, with no `Map.Entry` in sight. `BiConsumer` also has `andThen`, just like `Consumer`.

items: `lines(Map<String, Integer> scores)` returns one line `name=score` per entry, produced by a `BiConsumer` passed to `scores.forEach`. A missing score (a `null` value) is written as `-`.

`both(BiConsumer<K, V> first, BiConsumer<K, V> second)` returns a `BiConsumer` that runs `first`, then `second`, on the same key and value. If `first` throws, its exception reaches the caller and `second` does not run.

blocks.text: The lines follow the order in which the map itself iterates, one entry at a time, however large the map. Some maps (a `HashMap`) allow `null` values.

cases.says: Each entry becomes one name=score line.
The combined BiConsumer runs the first one, then the second, on the same key and value.
Lines come out in the map's own iteration order; nothing is sorted.
Map.forEach passes a null value through, and it is shown as a dash.
If the first BiConsumer throws, the exception reaches the caller and the second one does not run.
Even a large map is reported one entry at a time, in the map's own order.

concepts: Map.forEach hands each key and value to a BiConsumer, in the map's own iteration order.
Map.forEach passes a null value through when the map allows one, so the BiConsumer guards it.
